newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar seen solid but upside limited in Asia.
newsitem.headline: Dollar seen solid but upside limited in Asia.

text.p: The dollar is expected to be well-supported below 118 yen on buying on dips and bids from Japanese institutional investors in Asia, dealers said.
They added that bullish sentiment towards the dollar is expected to continue, but the U.S. currency's upside is likely to be limited unless fresh buying incentives emerge.
Mark sales against the yen in cross trade may also indirectly weigh on the dollar/yen rate, they said.
"We have recently tried to retest 119 yen a couple of times but failed. I don't see many fresh dollar purchases (at high levels) from traders," a trust bank dealer said.
He added that if sales of marks against the yen continue, that would put a lid on the dollar's rise against the yen.
A city bank dealer said, however, that Japanese investors are keen to pick up the dollar below 118 yen and this is likely to keep the dollar solid on the downside.

A possible further fall in Japanese market interest rates will keep traders reluctant to buy the yen aggressively, providing another factor to support the dollar, the city bank dealer said. On Monday, the dollar received a temporary boost against the yen in reaction to a drop in the yield of Japanese government bonds, which fell to a record low of 2.070 percent.
Profit-taking may cap the dollar's rise against the mark following a strong rally overnight, dealers said.
The greenback rose as high as 1.8730 marks in Europe on Monday, its highest since October 1989, amid growing expectations that interest rates will soon rise in the United States.
But profit-taking and rumours that Germany would soon allow its official interest rates to rise pushed the dollar from its lofty perch despite broad dollar bullishness in New York trade.
Dealers said further profit-taking in dollar/mark trade is likely, but the undertone of the mark remains weak.
